topic: Crocodile losing to Luffy at Alabasta was the luckiest outcome for him, not the worst
title: Losing To Luffy Is What Saved Crocodile
description: What if Crocodile's poisoned hook actually landed at Alabasta? He wins the kingdom and finds Pluton, and that's exactly what destroys him. Full breakdown in the long version.
comment: Which defeat actually cost Crocodile more: losing to Luffy, or everything that would have happened if he'd won?

lines.text: Crocodile needed to lose to Luffy. Here's why.

shot.fallback: desert warlord facing a young pirate

lines.text: What if his poisoned hook had actually landed clean that day?

shot.fallback: warlord striking with a hidden weapon

lines.text: Operation Utopia finishes. Alubarna falls. Cobra becomes a puppet king.

shot.fallback: desert king ruling with no real power

lines.text: Crocodile gets everything Baroque Works ever wanted: the kingdom, and Pluton's location.

shot.fallback: warlord standing over a conquered kingdom

lines.text: That's when the World Government stops seeing a Warlord, and starts seeing a liability.

shot.fallback: government officials marking a dangerous man

lines.text: They don't even need him defeated. Succeeding that well is the real threat.
So they strip his title and ship him to Impel Down anyway.

shot.fallback: warlord stripped of rank and imprisoned

lines.text: Same prison as the real story. Completely different reason: winning, not losing.
Beating the system never saves you from it. It just proves how dangerous you are.

shot.fallback: man caught by the system he beat

lines.text: So no, losing to a kid in a straw hat wasn't Crocodile's worst day.
Crocodile needed to lose to Luffy, because winning would have cost him everything else...

shot.fallback: desert warlord facing a young pirate, resolute

self_check.loop: last line loops back into line 1's claim with the reason attached
